newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat exports may hit 3.5 mln tns by end March.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat exports may hit 3.5 mln tns by end March.

text.p: Traders expect UK wheat exports to reach between 3.3 and 3.5 million tonnes by the end of March, according to the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority.
The figure refers to exports from the start of the July-June marketing year to date.

It represents a big jump on the previous year's performance. In 1995-96, the UK exported 2,591,070 tonnes by the end of March, an HGCA expert said. Exports for 1995/96 as a whole were 3,146,609 tonnes, she said.
In its Weekly Bulletin, the HGCA compares this level with the farm ministry export availability estimate of 4.2 million tonnes for the whole season.
It points out that "some 0.7 to 0.9 million tonnes would need to be exported in the last quarter (April-June) to prevent a large end-season stock carryover.
Over the past three seasons, last quarter UK wheat exports have averaged over 600,000 tonnes and in 1991-92 and 1992-93 they averaged one million tonnes, the HGCA said.

Even though some industry experts put this year's wheat export availability at less than the official estimate of 4.2 million tonnes, "UK supplies will need to remain competitive to maintain exports at relatively high levels during these months," the HGCA said.
